key_concept: Prokaryotic cells have 70S ribosomes (50S + 30S), may carry plasmids and have mesosomes, but they lack membrane-bound organelles such as peroxisomes.
steps: Statement (a): Prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S, made of a large 50S and a small 30S subunit. Correct.
Statement (b): Many bacteria carry plasmids. These are small, circular, extra-chromosomal DNA that give extra traits such as antibiotic resistance. Correct.
Statement (c): Mesosomes are infoldings of the plasma membrane seen in prokaryotes. They are linked to cell wall formation, DNA replication and distribution, respiration and secretion. Correct.
Statement (d): Peroxisomes are single-membrane-bound microbodies. They are found only in eukaryotic cells, and prokaryotes lack membrane-bound organelles. Incorrect.
So the correct statements are (a), (b) and (c), which matches option (4).
why_not_others: Options (1) and (2) each leave out a correct statement: (1) omits the 70S ribosome subunits and (2) omits plasmids. Option (3) wrongly includes peroxisomes, which are membrane-bound organelles absent in prokaryotes.
common_trap: Students sometimes drop statement (a) because they think '70S' and '50S + 30S' contradict each other. In fact S values are not additive, so 50S + 30S forms a 70S ribosome.
time_saving_tip: Rule out (d) first, since peroxisomes are membrane-bound and so cannot occur in prokaryotes. That removes option (3). Among the rest, only option (4) includes all three of (a), (b) and (c).
